item.title: ‘Swifties not going to like that one’: Taylor Swift gets called ‘very performative’ by NBA players
item.description: Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images The New York Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs to win the franchise’s first NBA title in 53 years. Predictably, the atmosphere for every game in Madison Square Garden was electric. Hollywood A-lister Timothee Chalamet led the charge, but as always, the stars came out to watch the Knicks throughout their playoff run. Some of the biggest stars in the world came out, including the HAIM sisters, Chalamet’s girlfriend, socialite Kylie Jenner, and even global pop sensation Taylor Swift. Unfortunately for Swift, the Knicks players might not respect Swift’s fandom. Knicks players Duece McBride and Tyler Kolek recently sat down for a game of 2K with the NBA 2K League on TikTok and were asked who the fakest celebrity fan they’d encountered was. “Maybe Taylor Swift?” Kolek thought out loud. “I don’t know if I’ve seen her at any other games.” “I would agree,” McBride said. “Swifties not gonna like that answer.” “Everyone else is usually solid,” Kolek added. “Like Ben Stiller, (Tracy Morgan); I guess she’s got a lot going on, so she can’t come all the time.” “You trying to save your *ss,” McBride said. “It’s a little performative.” Kolek and McBride aren’t the first ones to call Swift out as a fake fan. Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy had a message for the pop star during the Finals. “Taylor Swift, not a fan, she’s celebrating, I’m sick of her,” he said of her attending Finals games. “I just— the whole thing I hate. I hate it all. Like, I like Larry David, uh, Curb Your Enthusiasm. I like Seinfeld. I hate them. Scooter Braun, I’ve always hated him. Big T*ts McGee, Sweeney, Uh, where’s she from? Hater. What is Hailey Bieber doing at the game with Tate McRae? Tate, you’re from Canada. “I hate them all… I just hate New York Sports fans.” Maybe Swift will attend some regular-season games this year to prove that she’s not “performative.” The post ‘Swifties not going to like that one’: Taylor Swift gets called ‘very performative’ by NBA players appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: El Cerrito police expect to make 'multiple arrests' over HS football hazing
item.description: El Cerrito High School in El Cerrito, Calif. (Google Street View) El Cerrito police said Thursday they expect to make "multiple arrests" following an investigation into two years of alleged hazing in the city's high school football program. The El Cerrito Police Department said in a news release that it had received a report of alleged bullying and hazing at El Cerrito High School on Oct. 2. Through its subsequent investigation, which included interviews with witnesses and school staff and the discovery of video evidence, the department said it had identified 22 current and former students who are suspected of committing "battery, sexual battery, assault, false imprisonment, dissuading a victim, conspiracy, and stalking." The abuse had occurred between September 2024 and October 2026, the department said in the release. The investigation remains active, and detectives continue to evaluate evidence. In response to the allegations, the West Contra Costa Unified School District suspended the Gauchos football program for the rest of the 2026 season. The school district also said it is conducting its own investigation under Title IX. "No child should ever experience what our students have described," said WCCUSD Superintendent Cheryl Cotton said in a statement. "While we have worked to focus on accountability for the actions of individual players up until this point, new information has led to new decisions. We must now make the very tough call to immediately suspend the El Cerrito High football program in order to prevent any further harm and restore a safe learning environment for our students." El Cerrito police Capt. Lauren Caputo declined to offer further details in a phone call with SFGATE on Thursday morning, saying that because the investigation involved juvenile victims, he was prohibited from discussing the case further. It's the latest in an eventful few years for the El Cerrito football team. In 2024, it forfeited six games for using ineligible players, which ultimately led to head coach Jacob Rincon's ouster. Last year, under new head coach Tim Johnson, the Gauchos won a California International Federation state championship in the sport, going 13-2 and taking home the school's first state title. The Gauchos had gone 6-3 in the 2026 season so far and had their season finale scheduled for Friday night at De Anza High School in El Sobrante before the start of the North Coast Section playoffs next week. item.title: Former Angels GM Perry Minasian returns to the Braves organization, per report
item.description: Anaheim, CA - November 15: Angeles general manager Perry Minasian listens to a reporter's question after introducing Angels new manager Ron Washington during his introduction news conference at Angel Stadium in Anaheim Wednesday, Nov. 15, 2023. (Allen J. Schaben / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images) That sound you’re hearing blasting from Cobb County right now is the front office for the Atlanta Braves blaring a familiar tune from Thin Lizzy . Not too long ago, former Astros GM Dana Brown returned to the franchise as a senior adviser for amateur scouting. Now, former Angels GM Perry Minasian is returning to the Braves to work with Alex Anthopoulos once again. Bob Nightengale of USA Today was the first to report the news and Jesús Cano of The Athletic added on that Minasian is returning in the same role as Dana Brown, so those two will be working together. There’s not a ton to say here, other than it seems pretty exciting that the Braves are bolstering their front office with some proven (and familiar) figures around here. Both of these guys have worked well with Anthopoulos in the past and had success with the Braves as well, so hopefully we’ll be able to see them pick up where they left off in their new roles with Atlanta for the 2027 season. Brown was last season with the Braves in 2022, while Minasian will be returning after leaving following the 2020 season. If I had to guess, both executives were probably willing to take on their jobs as sort of a holding situation for another big job opening up in the future but that’s pure and total speculation on my part. The tangible part here is that their experience and familiarity should be a positive for the organization going forward — especially (as Gaurav Vedak mentions below) considering that the farm is also starting to look encouraging for the first time in a while. Ronit Shah, Dana Brown, and Perry Minasian managing a quickly developing Braves farm system that has two of the top 40 prospects in baseball. We are going to have some FUN in 2027. Let me interview them @Braves — Gaurav (@gvedak) November 6, 2026 So yeah, hopefully we’ll see this front office continue to be competent and get stuff done, as they will surely benefit from now having both Dana Brown and Perry Minasian back in the fold for the moment.

item.title: NEW Lutheran volleyball falls in state semifinal, while Bay Port wins first match
item.description: ASHWAUBENON – The Northeastern Wisconsin Lutheran girls volleyball program waited 19 years to earn a trip back to the WIAA state tournament. It will have to wait at least one more to get its first win on the big stage. NEW Lutheran had its season end in four sets against Central Wisconsin Christian in a WIAA Division 5 semifinal at the Resch Center on Nov. 5, losing 25-22, 21-25, 25-22, 25-20. It was the Blazers’ first loss in a best-of-five format in 2026 and came against the same team that ended their season in a sectional semifinal last year. Senior setter and Lakeland University commit Olivia Kirchner led NEW with a match-high 32 assists, senior outside hitter and Wisconsin Lutheran College commit Kiley Dhein had a team-high 13 kills and senior libero Meredith Lemke-Scott finished with 19 digs. “It was a great match,” said NEW coach Michael Schmidt, who is in his 14th season with the team and has more than 300 career wins. “I knew it was going to be a battle all the way through. We scouted them well. We knew what they were capable of, we knew what we were capable of. “Just having a chance to be here on the floor and lay it all out there, that was really great. Really awesome.” The Blazers trailed the Crusaders after one set, which was just the second set they had lost since regional play started. But it was nothing to panic about. NEW (33-12) dropped the first set to Florence in a sectional championship and responded by winning three straight to punch its ticket to state. It looked like it might happen again. The Blazers broke a 17-all tie in the second set on a kill by Paige Loock and extended the lead after two more kills from Dhein. The Crusaders (31-8) got to within 22-21, but NEW responded by scoring the final four points to even the match at one set. “In a match of five, that first set is so big,” Central Wisconsin Christian coach Dan TenNapel said. “They come back and win set two. That third set, when it’s tied 1-1, that just dictates so much of the match. It takes so much pressure off you, puts so much pressure on the other team.” It was Central Wisconsin Christian that put all the pressure back on NEW. It was cruising in the third set after taking a 19-12 lead, and even after the Blazers roared back to tie the score at 22, the Crusaders won the last three points to close out the set. “I think with how things got toward the end, it is hard to come back,” Schmidt said. “We were battling, battling, battling and then we just had too many errors at really inopportune times. “We had some net touches that didn’t go our way. We had some serves that didn’t go our way. It’s really hard to be successful when we are making errors ourselves.” The Crusaders took a 7-6 lead in the fourth set and never relinquished it, advancing to the title match on Nov. 7 against Turtle Lake. item.title: Green Bay Packers will continue to stick with Trey Smack despite rookie’s recent struggles
item.description: Beyond their running game, the Green Bay Packers must also find consistency in their kicking game if they have plans to become a legitimate Super Bowl contender this season. After letting go of Brandon McManus this summer, they have relied on Trey Smack , whom they traded up to in the sixth round during this year’s NFL Draft. While everyone expected there would be some growing pains with a rookie kicker, those concerns reared their ugly head in Week 8 against the Carolina Panthers, as Smack now leads the league with eight missed kicks (5 FGs, 3 PATs) – the most for a Packers kicker in the first eight games of a season since Max Zendejas had nine in 1988. Trey Smack’s Week 8 performance with the Green Bay Packers Oct 25, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Green Bay Packers kicker Trey Smack (28) watches a field goal miss during the first quarter against the Detroit Lions at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images Green Bay Packers kicker Trey Smack finished with three points after going 3-for-4 on his PATs. Overall, the Florida product has gone 11-for-16 on field goals (68.8 percent – good for 30th in the league) and 16-for-19 on PATs (84.2 percent – good for 31st in the league) for 49 points this campaign. However, he will be remembered more for his first attempt, when he hit a “doink” off the left upright in the first quarter after Tucker Kraft made it 6-3, which gave Carolina a sliver of hope. Fortunately for Green Bay, his early miss didn’t cost them, as Josh Jacobs and Matthew Golden scored two more touchdowns. Green Bay Packers remain committed to Trey Smack Aug 28, 2026; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Green Bay Packers kicker Trey Smack (28) during the game against the Arizona Cardinals at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images In a recent media availability, Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur is adamant about sticking with Trey Smack at kicker, despite his recent struggles. That said, Smack has to repay the team’s trust in him in the next few games. “I think he’s done a lot of good things,” LaFleur said of Smack . “The thing I like about Trey is he’s shown to bounce back. Never want to be in a bounce-back situation, but that’s football. You got to be able to be resilient and go out there and play the next play. It started off bad, obviously, this last game missing a PAT, and then he responded.” More Green Bay Packers news from Wisconsin Sports Heroics Green Bay Packers: 3 studs and duds as 2026 NFL season hits halfway point NFL expands investigation into Packers’ Josh Jacobs after three more women make allegations Green Bay Packers: Jordan Love is having an MVP-caliber season despite horrid offensive deficiencies

item.title: Tigers' top prospect won't play in Arizona Fall League All-Star Game
item.description: The Tigers' No. 1-ranked prospect's season is over. Zyhir Hope is finished playing in 2026, after a hectic year in which he was dealt from the Los Angeles Dodgers to the Tigers in the Tarik Skubal trade. He then played in the Arizona Fall League. Hope was named to the Arizona Fall League All-Star Game, which is scheduled for Sunday night. But he won't play in the game. The Tigers decided before sending him to the AFL that his season would end at the end of October. More: Three Tigers among finalists for American League Silver Slugger awards Hope, 21, played 16 games for the Scottsdale Scorpions in the AFL and slashed .241/.405/.293 with one home run and 11 RBIs. He walked 14 times and struck out 16 times. Hope was one of three prospects sent from the Dodgers to the Tigers for Skubal, the two-time Cy Young winner, in early August, along with right-handed pitchers River Ryan and Brady Smith. Hope, a left-handed-hitting outfielder, played 30 regular-season games for Double-A Erie after the trade, with six homers, 24 RBIs and eight stolen bases. Before the trade, he had 23 homers, 87 RBIs and 18 stolen bases for Double-A Tulsa in the Dodgers' organization. For the year at Double A, he slashed .287/.367/.513 with 29 home runs, 111 RBIs and 26 stolen bases (he was caught six times). He had 62 walks and 141 strikeouts in 124 games. More: Kevin McGonigle named Tiger of the Year by Detroit baseball writers Hope was an 11th-round pick by the Chicago Cubs in the 2023 Major League Baseball Draft, and was dealt to the Dodgers in January 2024. He is the No. 26-ranked prospect in baseball, according to MLB Pipeline, and is expected to make his major-league debut with the Tigers at some point in 2027, Tigers president Scott Harris said in late September. Hope likely will start 2027 at Triple-A Toledo. Ryan, the No. 3 Tigers prospect according to MLB Pipeline, made his Tigers debut in September , while Smith, the No. 9 prospect, is father away from the major leagues. He pitched in Single A in 2026. The AFL season ends Friday, with the All-Star Game set for 8 p.m. Sunday at Salt River Fields in Scottsdale. Hope was the only Tigers prospect selected to the American League's All-Star roster. Seven other Tigers participated in the 2026 AFL: Shortstop Bryce Rainer, the Tigers' No. 2-ranked prospect ; infielder John Peck; and pitchers Logan Berrier, Jalen Evans, Preston Howey, Maddox Long and Win Scott. tpaul@detroitnews.com @tonypaul1984 This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Tigers' top prospect won't play in Arizona Fall League All-Star Game

The Packers have been hit hard by penalty calls in recent weeks, and quarterback Jordan Love and his wife dressed up as blind NFL referees for the recently concluded Halloween celebration. item.title: Cardinals' Tyler Allgeier's recent play just hints at his potential
item.description: Arizona Cardinals running back Tyler Allgeier took charge over the Dallas Cowboys defense in Week 8 but this should only be a point of reference for what General Manager Monti Ossenfort already knew. Allgeier's 11 attempts and 147 rushing yards might may some marvel but it only reinforces the optimism of head coach Mike LaFleur regarding the offense's potential upside. LaFleur wants his offense to play with fuel and fire but most of their offensive possessions have stalled out due to negative plays and sacks allowed by former starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett. With quarterback Gardner Minshew taking over the most important leadership role on offense, the franchise can expect to see more ball distribution and decency overall. Allgeier knows that his ability to get those tough short-yardage gains and wear down opposing defenses late in games makes him an asset to LaFleur and the offense. LaFleur has the personnel to be productive and multi-faceted and the collective offensive output in Week 8 surely showcased that. On Sunday, the Cardinals kept the contest within striking distance and were able to finally feed off of Allgeier's epic 63-yard touchdown run in the final minute of the third quarter. Allgeier's ability to sway the game's momentum and ignite the turnaround is not something the Cardinals will take as a result of luck but rather it speaks to Allgeier's determination and outright preparation. As a tandem, Allgeier and rookie running back Jeremiyah Love could play as a staple for the franchise, and their complementary running styles create a duality that is needed for the team. Ultimately, Allgeier's services will be needed for the Cardinals to continue running a balanced offensive attack. The team's 33-point output in Week 8 wouldn't have come to pass if not for Allgeier. item.title: Devin Haney-Liam Paro welterweight unification official for Dec. 19 at Chase Center
item.description: Devin Haney drops Brian Norman Jr. on his way to winning the WBO welterweight title in November 2025. SAN FRANCISCO — Devin Haney’s homecoming has a date. The three-division champion and WBO welterweight titleholder will face IBF champion Liam Paro in a welterweight unification fight Saturday, Dec. 19, at Chase Center, Top Rank announced Thursday. Dec. 19 will be his second appearance at Chase Center, where he stopped the clock on Regis Prograis in December 2023 to become a two-division champion at 140 pounds. Now he looks to unify titles in a second weight class. Paro (28-1, 16 KOs), a native of Mackay, Australia, became a two-division world champion in June when he handed Lewis Crocker his first defeat by unanimous decision in Brisbane. He has made a habit of winning away from home. In June 2024, he outpointed Subriel Matias in Puerto Rico to capture the super lightweight world title. “My resume speaks for itself. item.description: ‘I Just Don’t Feel Like I’m Wrong’ — Ryan Clark Reveals What Nearly Pushed Him To Quit ESPN Job Before Controversial Firing Months before ESPN let him go during a commercial break on “NFL Live,” Ryan Clark was ready to leave on his own. He had a “First Take” appearance on his schedule, and he says ESPN told him he couldn’t work until he apologized for what he’d said about former LSU receiver Kyren Lacy. Clark thought he’d made up his mind. Then he went for a walk with his wife, Yonka. Ryan Clark Says ESPN Made an Apology a Condition of Working Speaking with Matt Barnes on “All the Smoke,” Clark recalled asking Scott Van Pelt at halftime of a “Monday Night Football” game if he could talk about Lacy on the postgame “SportsCenter.” Clark knew Lacy personally and wanted to address footage released by Lacy’s attorney. He said Van Pelt was comfortable giving him the time. Clark used the segment to defend Lacy and declare him innocent. The next day, according to Clark, ESPN executive Dave Roberts called and asked him to apologize. Clark told Barnes he pushed back because he believed he had accurately described the information he was working from. With “First Take” coming up, he told Yonka he was prepared to quit. “Because they told me that if I didn’t apologize, I couldn’t work,” Clark told Barnes . “And the next day, I was supposed to be on First Take. I said, ‘Babe, it’s not worth it to me to apologize for something that I just don’t feel like I’m wrong.’” Yonka urged him to reconsider. “Boo, I don’t think this is the hill for you to die on,” Clark recalled her telling him. He said he then asked ESPN’s public relations staff if he could write his own apology. According to Clark, the network initially wanted a written statement on social media. He wanted the chance to speak on air, as his colleagues had. item.title: LIV Golf timeline: 17 crucial events in the breakaway league's history
item.description: Bryson DeChambeau high fives fans at what turned out to be LIV Golf's final tournament in Indianapolis in August. Getty Images After five seasons, 62 tournaments and more than $5 billion in spending, LIV Golf is no longer . The upstart league changed the game in numerous ways, but perhaps most markedly, LIV’s influence normalized the idea of super-sized purses in professional golf, with the PGA Tour now regularly offering $20 million in its Signature Events, and the major championships nearly doubling their purse offerings since 2021 to keep pace. How did it all begin — and end? Below, you can follow a timeline of 17 crucial events that shaped LIV Golf’s history. OCTOBER 2021 Greg Norman announces that he has accepted the position of CEO for LIV Golf Investments , of which the majority stakeholder is the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia. MARCH 2022 LIV Golf officially announces a slate of eight 2022 events , beginning in London on June 9 at the Centurion Club. The prize money for the total series is set at a whopping $225 million. MAY 2022 Dustin Johnson signs with LIV for a reported $125 million. He is joined by up-and-comer Talor Gooch and European legends Sergio García, Lee Westwood, Ian Poulter and Martin Kaymer. JUNE 2022 Phil Mickelson signs a multiyear contract with LIV ahead of the league’s first tournament. Onsite, additional recruits are revealed: Patrick Reed, Bryson DeChambeau and Pat Perez. Weeks later, after the U.S. Open, Brooks Koepka joins too, along with Carlos Ortiz and Matthew Wolff. AUGUST 2022 Reigning Players and Open Champion — and then No. 2 player in the world — Cameron Smith joins LIV Golf , along with a handful of others: Marc Leishman, Joaquin Niemann, Harold Varner III, Anirban Lahiri and Cameron Tringale. MARCH 2023 Brooks Koepka wins the 2023 PGA Championship for his fifth career major title, becoming the first active LIV player to win a major championship. JUNE 2023 PGA Tour Commissioner Jay Monahan and Public Investment Fund governor Yasir Al-Rumayyan sign a five-page “framework agreement,” effectively ending litigation and announcing the intent to form a mutually beneficial new entity. item.description: THIS PICTURE IS OVER 14 YEARS OLD. TAKE MORE MASCOT PHOTOS. PLEASE. | Photo by Doug Pensinger/Getty Images Name: University of Detroit Mercy Location: Detroit, Michigan, which I hope was your first guess Founded: Detroit College got started in 1877 by the Jesuits for the usual “Jesuits like teaching” reasons, and they moved on to university status and a name change to University of Detroit in 1911. So, where does the mercy come in? That’s the Sisters of Mercy, the same group that opened up Mercyhurst as described in our last preview. They established Mercy College of Detroit in 1941. That was completely separate from University of Detroit until 1990 when the two institutions pushed all their chips into the table together. item.title: The rookie backstop
item.description: MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 03: Ethan Salas #8 of the San Diego Padres hits a single against the Milwaukee Brewers during the second inning in game one of the National League Division Series at American Family Field on October 03, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to our series grading every member of the San Diego Padres’ 40-man roster. The roster being evaluated is current as of Oct. 18, prior to the end of the World Series. Because of that, it will include players who will be free agents once the postseason concludes. Each player will be graded on their performance in the 2026 season, including the playoffs. That performance will be weighted based on how much time the player spent with the team (availability is the best ability). Ethan Salas Salas was signed by the Padres when he was just 16 years old. Although he was born in Florida, Salas grew up in Venezuela and qualified for international free agency. He was signed with a record-setting $5.6 million signing bonus. Since then, he has had a rollercoaster career. Salas was one of the brightest prospects in baseball before 2025 when a stress reaction forced him to miss most of the year. There was a worry he would never be the same. Overall Grade: B+ The backstop put those worries to bed quickly. Across 96 minor-league games in 2026, Salas slashed .296/.374/.488 with 10 homers and 31 extra-base hits. He was phenomenal in every way. He was promoted to Triple-A for the first time in his career and raked, hitting .326 with a .949 OPS in 24 games. That production led to speculation that the Padres might call up Salas to make his debut when rosters expanded. The rumors were true. Salas made his MLB debut to much fanfare as the youngest catcher to debut since Iván Rodríguez in 1991. He flew out to the deepest part of the yard in his first at-bat but went 0-for-4 that day. And the next day. And the next day. Salas started off his big-league career going a whopping 0-for-14. He finally recorded his first career hit on Sept. 13 against the San Francisco Giants, roping a triple. Salas never looked back after that. In the 10 games following, he hit .400 (10-for-25) with five RBI and 18 total bases. He also became the youngest catcher in MLB history to record a multi-homer game, swatting two against the Colorado Rockies. Salas will likely factor into the Padres’ catching group for 2027, sharing time behind the dish with Luis Campusano and Freddy Fermin. However, he could start the season in the minors if San Diego feels he needs some more time to develop.
